Many people know me as the first FEU law graduate to reach the highest court of our land
I became a justice of our Supreme Court, and later, the 21st chief justice of the Philippines, because I am an FEU graduate!
I said that with some levity but it contains grains of truth

what I have been, what I am, and what I will ever be, I owe first and foremost to our Lord Jesus Christ; second, to my parents; and third, to the education, training and upbringing I imbibed from FEU and the other schools
only five local schools have produced chief justices: UP, UST, Escuela de Derecho (now known as Manila Law College), Ateneo de Manila and FEU

Important people
the brilliant law Dean Jovito R. Salonga who took a personal liking to me and taught me what I call the FEU model of legal education
Fr. Michael Nolan, the erudite FEU chaplain, who taught me the rudiments of my Catholic faith. In turn, I helped Father Nolan (and the other school officials) build the FEU Chapel
Dr. Teodoro Evangelista, the epitome of dignity, prudence and fortitude
FEU taught me not only the arts and sciences, not only my religious faith, not only the law; it also gave me the opportunity to excel in student leadership
I was the youngest and first sophomore student to be elected president of the FEU Central Student Organization
My parents and my high school batch mates were surprised at how I metamorphosed from a shy introvert in Mapa High to an active student leader in FEU and in the nation
Michael M. Alba
Dr. Alba impressed me as perceptive, knowledgeable, purpose-driven, humble and possessed of distinct educational ideas designed for the 21st century
His ideas blended the legacies of the past with the exigencies of the present and the hopes of the future
More than five decades ago when I was enrolled at FEU, I marveled at the magic of black and white television

I believe Dr. Alba is the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution. Cheers!

stances.claim: Levity-with-grains-of-truth: CJP became a SC justice and the 21st CJ because he is an FEU graduate -- his career rests on what he imbibed from FEU and the other schools after Christ and his parents.

FEU taught CJP not only arts and sciences, religious faith, and the law, but also gave him the opportunity to excel in student leadership -- youngest-and-first-sophomore CSO president + co-founder of National Union of Students of the Philippines -- transforming him from shy introvert at Mapa to active student leader.

Dr. Alba's hour-long conversation impressed CJP as perceptive, knowledgeable, purpose-driven, humble, and possessed of distinct educational ideas designed for the 21st century -- blending legacies of the past with exigencies of the present and hopes of the future.
Alba is the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution -- board of trustees made a prudent choice; under him FEU will produce alumni more worthy than CJP's generation.

notable_anecdotes: The 15-centavo bus fare CJP's parents could not afford -- diverting him from his earned UP scholarship to FEU -- among the most quoted poverty-anecdotes in CJP's autobiographical material, recurring across columns.

The Oblation-promise narrative -- Mapa High batch of honor graduates promising one another at the UP campus to earn scholarships -- captures the pre-college aspiration before the bus-fare reality intervened.

Salonga taking 'a personal liking' to CJP and teaching the 'FEU model' (UP basic + Harvard MA + Yale doctorate) of legal education -- among the most explicit articulations of CJP's mentorship-by-Salonga.

The shy-introvert-to-active-student-leader metamorphosis -- CJP's youngest-and-first-sophomore presidency of FEU CSO + co-founding NUSP -- captured as a transformation his parents and Mapa batchmates were surprised by.
Father Nolan + FEU Chapel -- CJP helped build it in return for Catholic-faith rudiments instruction, the rare CJP biographical detail on his Catholic-faith formation outside Mapa-and-family context.
The five-CJ-producing-schools roster -- UP, UST, Escuela de Derecho (now Manila Law College), Ateneo de Manila, FEU -- used to anchor FEU's institutional pedigree.

The five-decades technology evolution catalog (black-and-white TV + telephone + telex + fax + cell phone + SMS + PC + Internet + email + iPad + smartphones + tablet + Google + GPS + YouTube + Magic Jack + Skype + Facebook + Viber + Twitter + Square) -- among CJP's most concentrated technology-evolution catalogs in the corpus.
Dr. Teodoro Evangelista as 'the epitome of dignity, prudence and fortitude' -- CJP's triple-virtue tribute to his FEU-era president (1952-1971), overlapping CJP's 1956-1960 stay.

Alba's credentials taxonomy -- academic (Stanford PhD) + economist (DLSU/UP professor, past Philippine Economic Society president) + educator (past DLSU dean) + internationalist (former WB/ADB/USAid consultant) -- comprehensive endorsement.
Title-quartet closing: 'the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution. Cheers!' -- the title's source revealed as the speech's closing toast.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban prints (in edited form) his Jan 28 2014 remarks at the investiture of Dr. Michael M. Alba as the 11th president of Far Eastern University, asking non-Tamaraw readers to bear with the audience. With characteristic levity-with-grains-of-truth he modifies the conventional framing: 'Many people know me as the first FEU law graduate to reach the highest court of our land' -- but he became a SC justice and the 21st CJ because he is an FEU graduate. What he has been, is, and will be, he owes first to Christ, second to his parents, and third to the education from FEU and the other schools -- noting that only five local schools have produced chief justices (UP, UST, Escuela de Derecho/Manila Law College, Ateneo de Manila, FEU). His Mapa High batch of honor graduates promised one another at the UP Oblation to earn scholarships there, and they did -- but unlike them, CJP could not study at UP because his impoverished parents could not afford the 15-centavo bus fare from their small Sampaloc apartment to UP-Diliman in QC, so they sent him to nearby FEU, which also granted him a scholarship. At FEU he met the important people who molded his young mind: Dean Alejandro R. Roces (later youngest education secretary at 37); the brilliant law Dean Jovito R. Salonga, who took a personal liking to CJP and taught him the FEU model of legal education -- a combination of Salonga's UP basic + Harvard MA + Yale doctorate insights; Fr. Michael Nolan, the erudite FEU chaplain who taught CJP the rudiments of his Catholic faith (in return CJP helped build the FEU Chapel); and Dr. Teodoro Evangelista, the epitome of dignity, prudence and fortitude, FEU president 1952-1971 (19 years overlapping CJP's 1956-1960 six-year stay among 36,000 students), who saw CJP often through student-leadership activities. FEU taught him not only arts and sciences, religious faith, and law, but also gave him the opportunity to excel in student leadership -- youngest and first sophomore president of the FEU Central Student Organization, co-founder and head of the National Union of Students of the Philippines, transforming him from shy introvert (Mapa) to active leader (FEU and the nation), surprising his parents and Mapa batchmates. He knows the FEU presidents who succeeded Evangelista (Nicanor M. Reyes Jr., Josephine C. Reyes, Felixberto C. Sta. Maria, Edilberto C. De Jesus, Lydia B. Echauz). He did not know Dr. Alba until last month when FEU chairman Aurelio R. Montinola III introduced them; in an hour-long conversation Alba impressed CJP as perceptive, knowledgeable, purpose-driven, humble, and possessed of distinct educational ideas designed for the 21st century, blending the legacies of the past with the exigencies of the present and the hopes of the future. CJP marveled five decades ago at black-and-white television and voices through telephone lines; since then have come telex, fax, cell phone, SMS, PC, Internet, email, iPad, smartphones, tablet, Google, GPS, YouTube, Magic Jack, Skype, Facebook, Viber, Twitter, Square. Times have rapidly changed; so have the scope, methods, needs and ends of education. FEU is fortunate to have a varied-interest president: academic (Stanford PhD), economist (DLSU/UP professor, past Philippine Economic Society president), educator (past DLSU dean), internationalist (former WB/ADB/USAid consultant). As a proud alumnus he welcomes Alba's investiture, congratulates the board of trustees for its prudent choice, and believes Alba is the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution. Cheers!
